summary: Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from 1987 to 1989 and completed her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna in 2002 under David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen is an Indologist and historian who earned her PhD from the University of Berlin and her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Her positions include faculty member at Halle-Wittenberg and researcher at the University of Berlin.

Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago in 1969. He served as a distinguished professor in humanities, religion, and literature at the University of Chicago from around 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago from 2001 to 2007 and was a professor of South Asian studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 2015.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a scholar of Sinology and history who studied under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak at Leiden University. He served at Leiden University as a lecturer in Chinese from 1946 and as professor from 1956 to 1975.

Anthony Kennedy Warder specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough. He served as lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and Chairman of East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford in 1995 under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.

Anthony W. Barber specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, completing his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984. He later held an attested post at the University of Calgary in 1998.
Antoine Lutz works in Buddhist studies and related fields. He earned his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Paris institutions under Sylvain Lévi, James Darmesteter, and Ferdinand de Saussure, later serving as professor at the Collège de France from 1905 to 1936.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a scholar of linguistics, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1806–1838) and held posts at INALCO, the University of Paris, and the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and INALCO, and served as Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832.

Anton Boller was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served at the University of Vienna from 1845, becoming extraordinary professor in 1850 and professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit in 1855.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his doctorate from the University of Berlin. He later served there as a Dozent from 1849 to 1852 and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Saint Petersburg and Berlin. He held posts at the Imperial Academy of Sciences from 1852 and taught at the Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy from 1860 to 1873.
Anton Westermann was a scholar of linguistics and history who completed his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig, where he served as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

Antonello Palumbo is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He held positions at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2004) and at SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

Antonino Forte was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at Hōbōgirin, the Italian School of East Asian Studies, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" from around 1989 to 2006.

Antonio T. de Nicolás was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who received his PhD from Fordham University in 1971. He served as a professor of philosophy at Stony Brook University from around 1968 to 1996.

Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned his PhD from Leiden University in 2010 under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar. He has served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
